clue.text: Self-evident right to probe wicked person's file

parts.note: a wicked person is a demon, and the possessive adds the S

indicators.note: a probe pushes into something, so the letter for right goes into the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: a file of data can be set out as a table, a list in rows

explanation.surface: An investigator has an obvious right to search a villain's records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'file' here is a set of records laid out in rows, not a folder or a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be shown or proved plainly is evident on its face.

clue.text: Doctor wine with drop of cognac? That's extreme

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

indicators.note: a drop is a tiny amount, so only the opening letter of cognac is taken

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: Spiking wine with brandy is going too far.
explanation.definitionFit: Drastic measures are severe or radical ones, taken to an extreme degree.

clue.text: When reversing, run over cat in drive

indicators.note: the pieces are read backwards, the motorist's manoeuvre doubling as the turnaround signal

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A driver backing out of a driveway accidentally hits a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: To motor is to travel by car, an informal verb for driving.

clue.text: Tell the authorities who revolutionary chap with short coat is? Not I

indicators.note: revolution is turning round, so the word for chap is read backwards

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: short means cut, so the last letter of the coating word is lopped off

parts.note: enamel is a coat of paint or glaze

indicators.note: says the following letter is taken away from the word is

parts.note: the word is, which loses one letter
the letter I

explanation.surface: An informer is asked to identify a radical in a short coat, but refuses to be involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who' is only a link. 'Not I' acts on the word 'is', leaving its S.
explanation.definitionFit: To name names is an idiom for informing on others, identifying culprits to police or officials.

clue.text: French movie star still to appear naked

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters of the word for still are removed

parts.note: static means still, not moving

explanation.surface: A French film star is persuaded to do a nude scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Tati was a French comic actor and director, known for Monsieur Hulot films.

clue.text: Guides an oddball in prayer

indicators.note: an oddball is eccentric, so the letters are scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: Guides lead a strange person in prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Agnus Dei, Latin for Lamb of God, is a liturgical prayer in the Mass.

clue.text: It's a sign Blair is corrupt

indicators.note: corrupt suggests something twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A political jibe: it is an omen that Tony Blair is dishonest.
explanation.definitionFit: Libra, the scales, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Heroic sailor, noble type, goes by car mostly

indicators.note: says one piece sits beside the next

parts.note: argon is a noble gas

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: an auto is a car

explanation.surface: A heroic seaman, of noble birth, travels by car most of the time.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argonauts were the Greek heroes who sailed with Jason on the Argo for the Golden Fleece.

clue.text: South American and European are neutral

parts.note: an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated A
N marks neutral, as on a gear stick or plug

explanation.surface: A political statement that South Americans and Europeans stay neutral.
explanation.definitionFit: Andean describes things from the Andes, the mountain chain of South America.

clue.text: Being without emotion, Papuan regularly eats fruit

indicators.note: something eaten goes inside, so the fruit sits within the picked letters
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of Papuan is taken

parts.note: its alternate letters
a tomato is botanically a fruit

explanation.surface: An unemotional person from Papua New Guinea snacks on fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters here (2nd, 4th, 6th), not the odd ones.
explanation.definitionFit: A robot-like person acting mechanically, with no feeling, is likened to a machine.

clue.text: One who wrote poems attributed to Howard, perhaps …

parts.note: a work credited to someone is by them
Ron Howard is the American actor and film director

explanation.surface: A poet whose verses are credited to someone called Howard.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries Howard into the next clue too.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Byron was the English Romantic poet who wrote Don Juan.

clue.text: … who blocks the toilet

indicators.note: something that blocks a pipe sits in the middle of it, so one piece goes inside the word the

parts.note: refers back to Howard in the previous clue, Ron Howard, so it stands for RON

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: Howard is the one clogging the lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to 10 across, so 'who' means the Howard named there, the director Ron Howard.
explanation.definitionFit: Throne is jocular slang for the lavatory seat or toilet.

clue.text: Surprisingly, cease devouring chop, a tender piece of meat

indicators.note: what is devoured goes inside, so the cutting word is placed within the rearranged letters
signals the letters of cease turn up in an unexpected order

parts.note: to lop is to chop off

explanation.surface: Someone unexpectedly stops eating a chop, a tender bit of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chop' looks like the meat being eaten, but it is the verb meaning cut.
explanation.definitionFit: An escalope is a thin boneless slice of meat, often veal, beaten flat and tender.

clue.text: Moist, like seafood?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, whimsically: resembling clams, the shellfish

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a playful coinage, clam plus the -my ending, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Clammy skin is unpleasantly damp; the joke reading treats it as clam-like.

clue.text: Nothing should interrupt Mahler's elaborate openings

indicators.note: an interruption breaks into the middle, so the zero goes inside the other letters
elaborate means intricately worked, so the composer's letters are reworked

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing should disturb the ornate overtures of Mahler's symphonies.
explanation.definitionFit: Armholes are the openings in a garment through which the arms pass.

clue.text: Idiot in distress cuddling agitated bear

indicators.note: to cuddle is to hold close, so the word for distress wraps round the other letters

parts.note: pain is distress or suffering

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, so the letters of bear are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A fool in trouble hugs an angry bear.
explanation.definitionFit: A pea-brain is a stupid person, whose brain is supposedly the size of a pea.

clue.text: Fool cut tail off fawn bird for an audience

indicators.note: the tail is the last letter, which is removed

parts.note: Bambi is Disney's famous fawn

indicators.note: an audience hears it, so the bird's name is taken by its sound

parts.note: the ouzel is a blackbird or a thrush-like bird

explanation.surface: A trickster docks a deer's tail, then puts on a bird show for spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: OUZEL said aloud sounds like OOZLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To bamboozle is to deceive or hoodwink someone, making a fool of them.

clue.text: Travelling around, receiving news in exchange for diamonds and spice

indicators.note: says one piece takes the place of the other in the reversed word
turned around, so the word for travelling is read backwards

parts.note: nomadic means wandering, travelling about
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds
read as the plural of N for new, so two Ns

explanation.surface: A merchant on the road gets word of a trade: spice for gems.
explanation.walkthrough: NOMADIC reversed is CIDAMON; the D (diamonds) is swapped for NN, 'news' taken as more than one N for new. 'receiving' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinnamon is a spice made from the dried bark of a tropical tree.

clue.text: Miles Jupp is hot when gyrating in desert

indicators.note: gyrating means spinning about, so the letters are whirled into a new order

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: The comedian Miles Jupp dances about while hot in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: Miles Jupp is a British comedian; here Miles gives only M.
explanation.definitionFit: To jump ship is an idiom for abandoning a post or cause, deserting it.

clue.text: Playing tricks, put sharp object in car

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other, the car holding the sharp object

parts.note: Jag is short for a Jaguar car
a pin is a sharp object

explanation.surface: A prankster leaves a spike in someone's car.
explanation.definitionFit: To jape is to play jokes or pranks, so japing is fooling around.

clue.text: See me tickle shoulders causing vomiting

indicators.note: the phrase shoulders the answer, bearing it within its letters

explanation.surface: Watch me tickle someone's shoulders until they are sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'causing vomiting' is an adjectival definition; the word also serves as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An emetic substance induces nausea and makes a person throw up.

clue.text: Advise governing body to be outspoken

indicators.note: spoken out means said aloud, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a council is a local governing body

explanation.surface: A recommendation that a council be blunt and frank.
explanation.definitionFit: To counsel is to give guidance or recommend a course of action.

clue.text: Advocate against the Euro?

parts.note: someone against the euro is in favour of keeping sterling, the pound

explanation.surface: A lawyer who campaigns against the single European currency.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as PRO-POUND, in favour of the British pound rather than the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: To propound is to put forward an idea for consideration, as an advocate does.

clue.text: Ring AA in dramatic performance

parts.note: a ring is round, like the letter O
two As: the first read as per, as in five pounds a day, the second as itself

explanation.surface: A phone call to the AA motoring service in the middle of a play.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a staged drama set to music.

clue.text: Black tea from country next to Uganda, originally

indicators.note: places one piece directly beside the other

parts.note: the Congo is a country in Africa

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the first letter of Uganda

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: Tea grown in a country neighbouring Uganda.
explanation.definitionFit: Congou is a Chinese black tea, a kind of leaf brewed without milk traditionally.

clue.text: Information on old American city

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Facts about an old city in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gen' is informal British slang for information or the facts.
explanation.definitionFit: Genoa is a port city in north-west Italy, birthplace of Columbus.

clue.text: Excited before golf

parts.note: ago means before now, in the past
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled ahead of a round of golf.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog means eager and expectant, full of excitement.

clue.text: Relative in Greece inebriated, doing a somersault

indicators.note: a somersault turns head over heels, so the hidden letters are read backwards
the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A drunken relation in Greece turns head over heels.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a sibling's daughter, a family member.

clue.text: Staring endlessly into same perverted publications

indicators.note: one piece goes into the middle of the other
perverted means turned from its proper course, so the letters of same are rearranged
without an end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: gazing means staring

explanation.surface: Staring endlessly at the same dirty magazines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perverted' colours the surface towards smut, but only signals that the letters of 'same' are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Magazines are periodical publications, issued weekly or monthly.

clue.text: Here, a calling to perform?

indicators.note: to perform is to act out, so the letters are put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: A musician's vocation leads to this famous stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the fodder with its signal and the definition: a famous venue where those with a calling to perform play.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnegie Hall is the celebrated New York concert venue, a goal for performing musicians.
